text:
maria gomez: FYI rolled canary of model v3-int4 to 5% for long-context workloads. Ran our goldset eval overnight and seeing systematic drift after ~18k tokens. Posting artifacts here.
samir patel: link to the run?
maria gomez: https://console.redwood/runs/rl-2026-03-18-2144 : results.json attached (summary: ppl up ~6% on longchat, token misalignment start at ~18000)
leo chan: do you mean the output starts repeating or is it hallucinating context-irrelevant tokens?
maria gomez: repetition + strange prefix bleed. Example snippet from the session:
```
... previous context ...
User: long prompt...
Model: ...answer...
Model: <duplicate chunk starting at token 18012> "the user asked about..." repeated
```
leo chan: that looks like a kv handoff boundary issue — shard swap / prefill mismatch could cause index offsets.
aj: infra-bot reported a shard swap at 2144511300 during the canary. infra-bot: "autoscaler: swapped 1->2 shards for sgd-pool-7"
infra-bot: deploy note: canary autoscale triggered at 2144511300; no OOMs. Rolling back not triggered.
dominique: did you run the same quantization recipe as the staging int8? v3-int4 used the new per-block dynamic scale. That could change rotary scaling semantics.
maria gomez: yes used quant-recipe vQ-2026-02-dynblock. I've attached comparison diffs against v3-int8.
samir patel: can you run a tight repro with `--max-seq 20000 --seed 42` and `LD_PRELOAD=./kv-debug.so` so we can log the kv index at handoff boundaries?
leo chan: add `ROPE_MODE=legacy` vs `ROPE_MODE=scaled` runs. If RoPE scaling changed, index computation across shards can drift.
aj: suggestion: run two runs A/B with prefill on/off. Prefill behavior is our usual culprit when rolling out new quant kernels.
maria gomez: running now: `./eval_goldset.sh --model v3-int4 --max-seq 20000 --seed 42 --out /tmp/run2144` (kicking off jobs 2144512350, 2144512365)
samir patel: nice, add `--dump-kv-frames` and a tiny script to diff kv positions across shard boundaries. If we see position mismatch it's definitely handoff.
dominique: also capture logits->tokens for the first 200 tokens after 18000 so we can compare where the divergence happens.
leo chan: quick hack: run with `KV_CACHE_WINDOW=16384` and `KV_CACHE_WINDOW=32768` to see if the boundary shifts. If the bug moves predictably it's an off-by-N in index math.
maria gomez: got first short run 2144512350 logs: https://console.redwood/logs/2144512350 — header shows `prefill_frames=on` but kv frames show an index jump from 18011->0 on shard swap.
aj: :eyes: that's textbook wraparound. Could be int4 packing math truncating higher bits on the index pointer.
samir patel: try a repro with the kernel env `INT4_INDEX_BITS=48` vs default 32 and see if it persists.
dominique: if changing index bits fixes it, we should include a regression test in the onboarding harness (goldset long-context) before any rollout >10%.
maria gomez: agreed — putting a hold on further rollout until we finish the two AB runs. If repro is stable we'll open a kernel PR.
leo chan: I'll add an integration test to eng-runtime that runs a 20k token goldset sample under quantized kernels in CI (nightly).
aj: tagging infra to keep an eye on canary: @infra-team please freeze autoscaling for v3-int4 until we confirm.
infra-bot: ack — autoscale freeze requested for v3-int4 canary. Will track until manual release.
samir patel: thanks, folks. After the `INT4_INDEX_BITS` run finish, post the diffs and I'll triage kernel vs runtime.
maria gomez: putting up a bug thread in issues: https://issues.redwood/INFR-2144 with initial artifacts. Will update here when jobs complete. :thumbsup:
_notes: Slack-style thread: short messages, code snippet, links, bot messages, @mentions and emoji. Single string with messages in chronological order.
